Meta Platforms Inc (META.O) 1st Impression: Ad Revs +23% Y/Y ex-FX on Holiday Strength & 1Q Guidance Better; ’26 CapEx & Expenses Higher Than Expected CITI’S TAKE Meta reported better-than-expected 4Q25 results with 1Q26 guidance calling for accelerating revenue growth, though higher-than-expected 2026 Expense & CapEx guidance. Total revenue of \$59.9 billion (+23% Y/Y ex-FX) came in 2.5% above FactSet consensus and \~1.5% above the high-end-of guidance led by advertising revenue growth +23% Y/Y ex-FX with ad impressions +18% Y/Y and pricing +6% Y/Y, with Meta noting a stronger holiday season overall along with continued benefits from R&R improvements and model changes. GAAP EPS was \$8.88, \~4% above our projection and \~8% above consensus. On guidance, 1Q revenue guidance range of \$53.5-\$56.5B is \~7% above consensus, though Meta provided ‘26 Expense guidance of \$162-\$169B, \~9% above our projections at the midpoint, and ’26 CapEx guidance of \$115-\$135B, \~13% above consensus at the midpoint. Key here, we believe significantly stronger 1Q revenue growth on continued strong engagement trends is likely to offset higher Expense and CapEx projections. • On the call, we’ll be focused on: 1) Product strategy and vision for MSL & TBD Labs as Meta builds Personal Superintelligence; 2) Meta’s evolving model strategy with Avocado & Mango and timing; 3) Continued momentum from Meta’s R&R changes and roadmap for continued benefits; 4) Progress with newer ad products and innovations; and 5) 2026E Expense, CapEx, and FCF details as investments continue to ramp. Overall Results—Revenue and OI Above Expectations: Revenue of \$59.9 billion (+24% Y/Y, +23% Y/Y ex-FX) came in \~2.5% above consensus. Operating income of \$24.7 billion (41.3% margin) came in \~3% above consensus and GAAP EPS of \$8.88 compares to consensus of \$8.21. • Family of Apps: Engagement and Revenue Above, Profitability Below Expectations: Family of Apps DAPs of 3.58 billion (+7% Y/Y) came in \~1% above our projection, revenue of \$58.9 billion (+25% Y/Y) was \~1% above our projection, led by +23% Y/Y advertising ex-FX growth, while Family of Apps OI of \$30.8 billion (52.2% margin) compares to our \$31.5 billion projection. • Reality Labs: Operating Losses Lower than Expected: Reality Labs revenue of \$955 million (-12% Y/Y) came in significantly above our \$542 million projection and RL Operating Losses of \~\$(6.0) billion compares to our \$(6.2) billion projection. Given Meta’s 2026 expense guide, recent 10% RL RIF and 30% Metaverse budget cuts, Meta now expects RL losses to be similar in ’26 (- \$19.2B), before improving in ’27 and going forward.

Meta guided 2026 Expenses to a range of \$162B-\$169B, +41% Y/Y at the mid-point and \~9% above our projections at the midpoint.

Meta Platforms Inc
Valuation
Our target price of \$850 is based on \~25x our 2027E GAAP EPS of \$33.79 and implies \~13x our 2027E EV/EBITDA. We justify our valuation methodology based on Meta’s user scale, growing engagement, product super cycle and AI opportunity, ads innovation, and revenue growth, and we’re watching investments and overall profitability.
Risks
Risks to our target price include: 1) Impacts from changes to ATT and IDFA could prove more difficult to overcome and structurally impact Meta’s advertising business; 2) Online advertising spend could decelerate faster than we anticipate; 3) Competition could prove to be more impactful than we anticipate; 4) Meta may not be able to achieve meaningful contributions from its investments in non-advertising businesses (metaverse). 5) Adverse economic and/or consumer spending trends could hinder advertising spend; and 6) Regulatory pressures on anti-trust, data, and privacy practices could adversely impact on performance.

Guide to Citi Research Fundamental Research Investment Ratings: Citi Research stock recommendations include an investment rating and an optional risk rating to highlight high risk stocks. Risk rating takes into account both price volatility and fundamental criteria. Stocks will either have no risk rating or a High risk rating assigned. ETR is the sum of the forecast price appreciation (or depreciation) plus the dividend yield for a stock within the next 12 months. The target price is based on a 12 month time horizon. The Investment rating definitions are: Buy (1) ETR of 15% or more or 25% or more for High risk stocks; and Sell (3) for negative ETR. Any covered stock not assigned a Buy or a Sell is a Neutral (2). A Catalyst Watch or STV Upside/Downside call will automatically expire at the end of the specified 30/90 day period. The Catalyst Watch will also be automatically removed if share price performance (calculated at market close) exceeds 15% against the direction of the call (unless over-ridden by the analyst). The analyst may also remove a Catalyst Watch or STV call prior to the end of the specified period in a published research note. A Catalyst Watch/STV Upside or Downside call may be different from and does not affect a stock’s fundamental equity rating, which reflects a longer-term total absolute return expectation. For purposes of FINRA ratings-distribution-disclosure rules, a Catalyst Watch/STV Upside call corresponds to a buy recommendation and a Catalyst Watch/STV Downside call corresponds to a sell recommendation. Any stock not assigned to a Catalyst Watch Upside, Catalyst Watch Downside, STV Upside, or STV Downside call is considered Catalyst Watch/STV No View. For purposes of FINRA ratings distribution-disclosure rules, we correspond Catalyst Watch/STV No View to Hold in our ratings distribution table for our Catalyst Watch/STV Upside/Downside rating system.
